clue.text: What we may have to reduce to meet the electricity bill

definitions.text: What we may have to reduce to meet the electricity bill

parts.words: What we may have to reduce to meet the electricity bill
parts.note: read as a bank statement: the running total in the everyday bank balance falls when we pay for power, while the surface suggests cutting usage of electric flow

explanation.surface: A household cutting back on power use to afford the electricity bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like electric flow being used less; it is the everyday cheque account whose balance drops when the bill is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday bank holding from which bills are paid is what shrinks when the electricity charge goes out.

clue.text: Utterly confused child I tucked into a new cot

indicators.note: tucked into tells us the letter I is placed inside the rearranged letters
new signals the letters of a cot are made anew in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child being tucked up into a brand new cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for the two words before it, and 'tucked into' places the lone letter inside that rearrangement; CH for child is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in total disorder, a shambles, is utterly confused.

clue.text: Revolutionary idea for increasing agricultural production

definitions.text: Revolutionary idea for increasing agricultural production

parts.words: Revolutionary idea for increasing agricultural production
parts.note: revolutionary is read literally as turning in a cycle: fields are planted with different crops in a repeating sequence to keep soil fertile

explanation.surface: A radical new scheme to boost farm output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a radical breakthrough; here it means going round in a cycle, as farmers vary what each field grows year by year.
explanation.definitionFit: Cycling different plantings through fields each season keeps soil fertile and so raises farm yields.

clue.text: Timber producers that have had a bad time in recent years

definitions.text: Timber producers that have had a bad time in recent years

parts.words: Timber producers that have had a bad time in recent years
parts.note: timber producers are trees, and the bad time is the Dutch disease spread by beetles that killed most of a familiar British hedgerow species

explanation.surface: Lumber companies going through a lean patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timber producers' reads as firms; they are trees. Dutch elm disease destroyed most of Britain's elms from the late 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: These trees yield wood and were ravaged by Dutch disease, a fungus carried by beetles.

clue.text: It repeatedly turns up with an old master

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the doubled letters read from bottom to top
repeatedly says the word it is written down twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painting that keeps surfacing alongside an Old Master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the word, and in a down clue 'turns up' reads that doubled pair from bottom to top; 'old master' covers great European painters before about 1800.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance painter is one of the great European painters called old masters.

clue.text: Meets with success or fails as a bronco buster?

definitions.meaning: a plan that works out is said to succeed in this phrase
a rider who fails to stay on a bucking horse falls from its back

explanation.definitionFit: A scheme that succeeds works out well; a rodeo rider who fails tumbles from the saddle.

clue.text: Not employed in the wrong position

definitions.meaning: without a job, lacking a post

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a post means jobless; being misplaced means sitting where something should not be.

clue.text: One must do everything possible to leave it

definitions.text: One must do everything possible to leave it

parts.words: One must do everything possible to leave it
parts.note: the idiom for trying every possible avenue is to leave no rock unflipped, so making every effort is how one leaves it

explanation.surface: Advice that you must try every option before departing.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'leave no stone unturned' means try everything; the clue turns it round, so doing everything is how you leave it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a search so thorough that not a single rock is left unflipped.

clue.text: Break a record? Get away with you!

definitions.meaning: to better a record time or score is to surpass it
a brusque command telling someone to go away

explanation.definitionFit: Surpassing a record means outdoing it; telling someone to clear off is the slang command.

clue.text: From which one may get a motorway dish or a car rug?

definitions.text: From which one may get a motorway dish

parts.note: auto is a short form of automobile, a car
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A motorway services stop selling meals and travel blankets.
explanation.walkthrough: An automat is a vending-machine restaurant; the dish comes from a coin-operated hatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated self-service eatery dispenses food from machines, the kind found by a roadside.

clue.text: A French artist returns it en masse

indicators.note: en is French for in, so the reversed word sits within the French word masse

parts.note: taken as written, from the French phrase en masse

indicators.note: returns tells us the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A French painter giving back a crowd's worth of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'en masse' looks like one French phrase, but 'en' is the French for in and acts as the container signal, while 'returns' turns the little word round before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a leading French painter of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: What the ballet-dancer wore for the African bishop

definitions.meaning: a stiff short skirt of layered net worn by ballerinas
Desmond ..., the South African Anglican archbishop

explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's stiff net skirt shares its name with the famous South African churchman Desmond.

clue.text: Dicky in evening dress?

parts.note: a dicky is a detachable starched shirt piece worn under a dinner jacket, giving the look of a whole shirt

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky turning up in black tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a man's name; it is a detachable starched shirt-front worn with evening dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A dicky is a separate bib that imitates a whole shirt, a pretend facade.

clue.text: Plight of a flooded mine powerless to operate internally?

definitions.text: Plight of a flooded mine powerless to operate internally?

parts.words: Plight of a flooded mine powerless to operate internally?
parts.note: a flooded pit cannot be dug or run, and the clue also hints at the words un- and work around a word for a pit pump, describing something that cannot operate

explanation.surface: A colliery flooded and without power, unable to run its inner workings.
explanation.walkthrough: A flooded mine cannot be worked, so it is literally impractical to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impractical that cannot function is like a flooded pit that miners cannot dig.

clue.text: Diadems not usually worn in the Civil Service

definitions.text: Diadems not usually worn in the Civil Service

parts.words: Diadems not usually worn in the Civil Service
parts.note: civil servants are servants of the monarchy's state, yet they do not wear royal headgear

explanation.surface: Office workers seldom turning up in tiaras.
explanation.walkthrough: British civil servants are servants of the Crown, though none wears one.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal headpieces are diadems, and the state that civil servants serve is named after one.

clue.text: Frolicsome faun left with a great deal of money

definitions.text: with a great deal of money

indicators.note: frolicsome means playful and skipping about, so these letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A playful faun departing, carrying a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy, rich person is one with plenty of cash.

clue.text: Carried out a grave commitment

parts.note: grave is read literally as a burial plot, so the commitment is a body consigned to the earth

explanation.surface: Fulfilled a serious undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave commitment' reads as a serious promise; it is a body committed to a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Burying a body is committing it to a grave.

clue.text: Put the case for sterling?

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, meaning in favour of
the pound is the unit of British sterling currency

explanation.surface: Arguing in support of the British currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is PRO and 'sterling' the POUND, Britain's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an argument or theory is to advance a case.

clue.text: Put outside a stately mansion

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for put goes around the letter a

parts.note: to put something is to place it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being thrown out of a grand mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is PLACE, which goes 'outside' A.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand official residence, a royal or stately mansion.

clue.text: A candlestick that could be fine at Oxford

definitions.meaning: at Oxford colleges, a forfeit imposed for breaches of dining etiquette, often downing a tankard of ale

explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford a sconce was a penalty imposed at dinner for breaking etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall-mounted candle holder shares its name with an old Oxford college penalty of drinking ale.

clue.text: On the day of decision his favourite gets cross

definitions.text: On the day of decision his favourite gets cross

parts.words: On the day of decision his favourite gets cross
parts.note: on polling day a voter marks his chosen candidate with a cross, so the favourite is crossed rather than angered

explanation.surface: A man's pet becoming angry on a big day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets cross' suggests anger; it is the X marked on a ballot paper beside the voter's chosen candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter on election day marks an X beside the candidate he prefers.

clue.text: First principle followed by an inhabitant of a divided country

indicators.note: followed by says the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: a germ is the seed or first principle of something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A basic idea being taken up by someone in a split nation.
explanation.walkthrough: When the clue was set, Germany was divided into East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Germany, then split into East and West, was a citizen of a divided country.

clue.text: Orthodox Sikh employed in the inland waterway service?

definitions.text: Orthodox Sikh employed in the inland waterway service?

parts.words: Orthodox Sikh employed in the inland waterway service?
parts.note: an observant Sikh never cuts his hair, so he preserves his tresses, and canal staff operate the gates that raise and lower boats

explanation.surface: A devout Sikh with a job on the canals.
explanation.walkthrough: Orthodox Sikhs do not cut their hair, so one keeps his locks; on a canal the same name is given to the person who operates the lock gates.
explanation.definitionFit: On canals, the worker who operates the gates that move boats between levels holds this job.

clue.text: In no doubt about following us back

indicators.note: following says the word for about comes after
back says the word us is written in reverse

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Being certain about tailing us on the way back.
explanation.definitionFit: Being certain means having no doubt.

clue.text: I go around after a special discount

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the letter a
around signals the letters of I go are moved about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone shopping around for a special bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I GO to GIO, placed 'after' A.
explanation.definitionFit: An agio is a premium or charge on exchanging currency, a financial percentage reckoned in trade.

clue.text: Come down with a vengeance on undignified clothing?

definitions.text: Come down with a vengeance on
definitions.meaning: to hit hard or punish severely

explanation.definitionFit: To hit someone hard is slang for punishing them; the same slang word means gear or clothes.

clue.text: Foreign minister whose line of defence proved ineffective

definitions.text: Foreign minister whose line of defence proved ineffective

parts.words: Foreign minister whose line of defence proved ineffective
parts.note: a French war minister gave his name to the fortified border which the German army simply went round in 1940

explanation.surface: An overseas politician whose argument fell flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line of defence' sounds like an argument; it is the fortified frontier line of France, bypassed in 1940.
explanation.definitionFit: André Maginot was the French war minister whose name went to the fortified line bypassed in 1940.

clue.text: Form of procedure followed by rock-climbers in rising numbers?

definitions.text: Form of procedure followed by rock-climbers in rising numbers?

parts.words: Form of procedure followed by rock-climbers in rising numbers?
parts.note: climbers going up in sequence follow a sequence, and numbers rising means the arrangement smallest to largest

explanation.surface: The routine climbers follow when many go up at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Climbers go up in a set sequence, and a list of numbers rising from smallest to largest has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers arranged from smallest to largest are in this sequence, as climbers going up are.
